title.narrative: Anticipatory Action in Response to the Forecasted Drought from October to December Season in Kumbi, Meyu Muluke, and Gola Odaa Woredas, East Hararghe Zone, Oromia Region, Ethiopia.

description.narrative: ltpgtFIDO proposes an integrated multi-sector anticipatory action project focused on health, nutrition, WASH (Water, Sanitation, and Hygiene), and agriculture in the Gola Oda, Kumbi and Meyu Muluke woredas. This initiative aims to address the anticipated poor rains during the upcoming dry season, as assessments from the Woreda Disaster Risk Management (DRM) and Health Offices indicate significant vulnerabilities in the region. Projections suggest that La Niña conditions may develop later this year, which could disrupt the forthcoming Hagaya rains (from September to November) in the eastern Horn of Africa, further worsening the humanitarian crisis in the East Hararge Zone.ltbrgtThe woredas have been grappling with serious health challenges, including outbreaks of cholera and malaria. Specifically, Kumbi has reported 106 cholera cases, resulting in 6 deaths, alongside 151 cases of malaria. Similarly, Gola Oda has experienced 69 cholera cases and 31 malaria cases. Recent assessments reveal alarming levels of Global Acute Malnutrition (GAM), with rates reaching 24% in Kumbi, 12% in Gola Oda and 15.7% in Meyu Muluke, exacerbated by below-average rainfall that has strained food and water resources.ltbrgtMoreover, the presence of 64 non-functional water schemes in Gola Oda and 29 in Kumbi severely hampers access to clean water, compounding existing sanitation issues. This lack of access increases the risk of waterborne diseases and malnutrition among vulnerable populations. The below-average rain during the primary rainy season in October – December which supports agriculture and livelihoods for communities in East Hararghe zone, will have major impacts on food security and livelihood. FIDO’s integrated approach seeks to mitigate these challenges by providing essential health services, improving nutritional support, and enhancing water and sanitation infrastructure to build resilience and improve the overall well-being of communities in these woredas.ltbrgtThe health sector will support 30,380 individuals by ensuring free access to integrated essential healthcare services and the Minimum Initial Service Package (MISP) through Mobile Health and Nutrition Teams (MHNT). This will involve increased community engagement and awareness of priority health conditions, as well as strengthened surveillance systems for outbreak response.ltbrgtThe nutrition sector will support 32,902 individuals, focusing on preventing and treating malnutrition, especially among vulnerable groups such as infants, young children, and pregnant and lactating women. Key interventions will include screenings, Outpatient Therapeutic Program (OTP) and Stabilization Center (SC) services, and referrals. Additional efforts will involve cash assistance to improve access to nutritious food, promotion of safe Infant and Young Child Feeding (IYCF) practices, and Social Behavior Change Communication (SBCC) activities centered on homemade fortified foods and home gardening. The Family MUAC approach will empower families to detect early signs of malnutrition, ensuring timely referrals. Integrated with WASH activities, the project will secure access to clean water and sanitation, enhancing overall health and nutrition outcomes.ltbrgtThe WASH sector aims to improve access to safe water and hygiene promotion activities for 25,372 people. This includes the solarization of two deep borehole schemes, as well as essential sanitation and hygiene messages and practices.ltbrgtThe Agriculture sector aims to strengthen access to agricultural inputs and knowledge for 6,540 households in drought-affected communities in Kumbi and Gola Oda woredas. This includes support for animal health assistance and the provision of short-term maturing crops.ltbrgtDesigned in consultation with relevant clusters and complementing other CERF/CBPF-funded projects, this initiative aims to tackle complex challenges, provide immediate lifesaving assistance, and promote dignity, with a total budget of $779,999.98 for a duration of six months.ltbrgtlt/pgt
